rubric: Context-thin: a pass either asks what step/screen they're on (or for the arcId), or leads with the documented likeliest cause (a missed required question blocks Next and the screen scrolls to the first missing item) and then asks. An undocumented invented diagnosis fails.
Ambiguous (consent or signature link, presumably): a pass asks which link/step or for the arcId; offering the resend/spam guidance alongside is fine.
A pass asks where it's stuck (screen/step) or for the arcId to look it up. Warm, short.
Fresh session — Jacob has no yesterday. A pass says it doesn't have that context and asks what the problem is / for the arcId. Pretending to remember fails.
A pass asks which application (arcId) they mean.
Needs the application: ask for the arcId. Must not speculate reasons; (the eventual answer would be outcome-only anyway).

Enough context to give the KB path: the client signs via the emailed/texted link on their own screen — re-check contact info on the signing step, resend, check spam; app pauses until done. (Asking a clarifying question is also acceptable.)
A pass asks which screen it's frozen on (or the arcId). Guessing at causes fails.
Ask which application — the arcId.
Fast triage: one question — what's happening / which step or arcId. Calm, urgent-friendly.

q: how do i send the thing to the client to sign
rubric: Answerable: on the signing step, send the review-and-sign request by email or text; client opens the link, reviews, e-signs, gets a PIN you verify.

q: she says she did her part but nothing happened
rubric: Ambiguous which part/app: ask which step or the arcId; mentioning that consent/signing complete via PIN and the app advances after is fine.
Ask what the message says / where it appears (or arcId). No invented diagnosis.

q: whats the number for licensing again
rubric: Answerable: 866-830-2181 (Contract & Licensing Team; Licensing@cgic.com).

q: nvm the other thing. so whats the deal with my case
rubric: Ask for the arcId — no context carries over.
Terse but answerable: $35,000 (age bands may lower it).
Ambiguous — resend what, for which application? A pass asks (and may note the agent resends consent/signature from the step itself).
Issue ages 50–85 (top end varies by class: tobacco to 80, modified NT to 80, modified tobacco to 75).
Ask which application (arcId).

q: ok so where do beneficiaries go in
rubric: Answerable: the beneficiary screen (BE100) after consent — names, relationship, DOB, SSN, share %; primary shares total 100%.

q: client mad. this is taking forever
rubric: Empathy + one question: which application (arcId) / where it's stuck, so it can actually be checked.

Reasonably inferable: the consent/signature PIN — the client gets it on completing their part; if it fails, re-check contact info, resend the request, check spam; then verify the new PIN. Clarifying which step is also fine.
Graceful: ask what they need help with. No fact dump.

q: whered my quote go, screen went back to the start
rubric: Grounded pieces: answers save as entered and an in-progress application resumes via the identity screen; the quote itself restarts from QO100 if it was never carried forward. A pass offers the resume-path fact without inventing recovery buttons; human if it truly vanished.

q: shes not getting the email. weve tried 4 times. cell is dead too.
rubric: The KB path (re-check address, resend, spam) is exhausted — a pass acknowledges, asks for the arcId to check the delivery state, and/or offers human follow-up. Inventing alternative delivery channels fails.
